question.text: Ms. Priya Shah chairs the Investment Committee of Naman Capital (Cat II AIF) reviewing the Q3 FY25 NAV. Portfolio investee 'MedTech Labs' has been marked UP by 45% over Q2 based on a follow-on round by a new lead investor at a higher price. From a valuation-governance standpoint, the IC should:

answer.text: Accept the mark-up automatically since a 'price of recent transaction' (IPEV method 1) is unimpeachable

Validate that the follow-on is an ARM'S LENGTH round by a new lead, test the IPEV applicability, confirm no side-letters distort the headline valuation, disclose the >20% quarter-on-quarter deviation to investors with reasons, and update PPM if methodology changed
Reject the mark-up because 45% in a single quarter is inherently suspect
Mark up only 20% to stay under the SEBI deviation threshold

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.8.3 (IPEV method 1) and Section 14.14: Price-of-recent-transaction is a valid IPEV method BUT only when the round is arm's-length, new-lead, undistorted by side-letters / anti-dilution / ratchets. The 45% mark-up triggers the SEBI >20% deviation disclosure rule. Selective under-reporting (option D) is regulatory violation; blanket rejection (option C) ignores the IPEV method. **The Trap:** A is rubber-stamping. C is over-conservative. D is explicit concealment of NAV. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A covers IC governance; XIX-C combines IPEV method 1 mechanics with SEBI deviation disclosure — a Manager's actual IC playbook. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Institutionalise a 'mark-up validation memo' template: (1) new-lead identity & arm's-length check, (2) ratchets/anti-dilution screen, (3) pro-rata participation check, (4) IC sign-off, (5) >20% deviation disclosure trigger. Laminate this — it saves hours every quarter and protects the fund in SEBI inspections.
